text.p: A Mashonaland team containing only five fulltime cricketers inflicted an embarrassing seven wicket defeat on England with a day to spare in their four day match at Harare Sports Club on Thursday.

Mashonaland scored the 98 runs they needed for victory after a second batting failure by England against an attack spearheaded by English county professional James Kirtley who has played only six first class games for Sussex.

Kirtley, who took five for 53 in the first innings, removed opener Nick Knight for three and Alec Stewart for a third ball duck to have England at four for two as they began their second innings 83 runs in arrears.

Zimbabwe test leg spinner Paul Strang and part time cricketer Gary Brent took over, claiming four wickets apiece as England were bowled out for 180. The defeat was the second in succession for captain Mike Atherton's tourists. They were beaten by five wickets by a President's X1 at the same Harare Sports Club ground on Sunday.
Atherton made only seven to add to his first innings two (he scored a duck on Sunday) but he would make no excuses.
"They played better than us -- they have deserved to win the match but this game has gone now," Atherton told reporters.
"We are all confident players. We all have records that prove we are good players and we just need some time in the middle.
"I haven't been at the crease long enough to find out what sort of form I am in but my record speaks for itself.
"It's taken us longer than anticipated to click into form. We all need overs under our belts."
England's prolonged resistance came from the middle order.
John Crawley looked in good form scoring 74 in 171 minutes before straight driving Brent to mid off and Nasser Hussain made 39 before he was adjudged lbw to Strang.
The pair shared a fourth wicket partnership of 76 but once they were separated wickets fell regularly.
England's lead of 97 looked indefensible but two quick wickets from Alan Mullally to reduce the home side to 11 for two raised hopes.
However, a second successive half century from Zimbabwe test skipper Alistair Campbell (53 not out) and 34 from first innings centurion David Houghton safely negotiated Mashonaland to their target.
"There's lots to be worked on and we need as much cricket as we can get," added Atherton.
England's request for a one day match against the same opposition on Friday was declined. They will have a practice session at the Alexandra Sports Club pitch in Harare instead.
They are next in action against a Matabeleland X1 in a one day match in Bulawayo on Sunday.
